passage:
Teacher's note, Class 4, Tuesday. At recess Baljeet stood alone by the water tank, turning a pebble in his hand. He has done this for a week. I was about to step in when Payal, running out with the football, stopped. “We need a goalkeeper. Baljeet, want to be it?” No speech, no fuss. Baljeet's face changed. He ran to the goalpost and stayed there all recess, shouting “Save!” once so loudly that everyone laughed, kindly.

What I did next: I stayed back and let them play. In the afternoon I quietly asked Payal what made her ask. “He looked like he wanted to,” she said. I'll keep mixing the football teams each week.

qa.q: Where was Baljeet standing alone at recess?
qa.a: Baljeet stood alone by the water tank, turning a pebble in his hand.

qa.q: What might Baljeet have felt when Payal asked to be the goalkeeper?
qa.a: Baljeet probably felt surprised and glad to be wanted, shown by the change in Baljeet's face and the loud shout.

qa.q: What choice did the teacher make at recess, and why might it help?
qa.a: The teacher stayed back and let the children play, so the invitation stayed ordinary and unforced.

qa.q: What might Payal have been thinking when asking Baljeet?
qa.a: Payal saw that Baljeet looked as if Baljeet wanted to play and simply acted on it, with no big plan.

grounding: A child invites a lone child into a game without fuss, and a teacher's note records how it changed the school day for the one included.

passage:
Monday. At recess we were playing a running game, me, Sneha, Ruchi and two others. Tejas was sitting by the tree again, drawing in the dust with a stick. I don't know why I did it, but I called, “Tejas, we need one more! Come!” Ruchi shrugged. Sneha said, “Okay.” Tejas looked up as if he thought I was talking to someone else. Then he ran over so fast he tripped, and everyone laughed, the nice kind. He was really good at being the catcher. At the bell he said “Thanks” very quietly.

Tomorrow I'm going to call him again.
— Afreen

qa.q: What was Tejas doing by the tree?
qa.a: Tejas was drawing in the dust with a stick.

qa.q: How did Tejas feel when Afreen called him to join the game?
qa.a: Tejas felt surprised and eager, looking up as if the call were meant for someone else and then running over so fast he tripped.

qa.q: What small choice did Afreen make that changed Tejas's recess?
qa.a: Afreen called out that they needed one more and invited Tejas without fuss.

qa.q: How might Afreen have felt when Tejas said "Thanks" very quietly at the bell?
qa.a: Afreen probably felt pleased and glad about calling Tejas over, which is why Afreen plans to call Tejas again tomorrow.

grounding: A child invites a lone child into a recess game without fuss, and a small act of inclusion changes the day.
